purpose: Measure the end-to-end cost, retained eligible accesses and amortization of constructing one ELF-bound site profile on the first execution of an unseen program.

population.calibration: For each of six executable digests, use exactly one previously unused calibration execution with the full live sampler. Use only its single schema-2 receipt. Retain its input, live clock, output, sample and generated profile. There are no native references or warmup trials.
population.holdouts: Use Aonohako #154 integer, branch and rep_fill /2 and /4, mod_inverse and branch_scan /2, plus path_switch/same and path_switch/switch. Freeze the file-by-file case manifest before provisioning. Never retrain on held-out executions.

order: Six first-run calibrations followed by balanced live/full/profiled trials on ten held-out input cases. Six scored repetitions per case and arm, paired by input and repetition. Run on one pinned AMD Milan logical CPU, with the same ELF, live budget, CPUID profile, child/observer placement and DynamoRIO settings within every pair.
profile_rule: Rank eligible main-module offsets by their visit counts in the one complete calibration receipt, descending, breaking ties by increasing offset. Select the shortest prefix covering at least 95% of calibration visits or stop after 64 sites. Persist the sorted offsets and source receipt/input/ELF identities. Validate each held-out lookup against the actual ELF digest. Account for the actual selection, write and lookup times.
integrity: Validate the complete live-mode process receipt and its exact terminal clock in every arm. On each held-out input, the profiled (offset, visits, completed pairs) vector must match the exact projection of the corresponding full run onto the frozen ELF offsets. Report all discrepancies. Near/far counts and byte spans outside hand-counted controls may vary with addresses in separate processes. Reconcile every schema-2 sample, and compare these fields separately. For the deliberately switched control use the independent hand-counted site and stdout oracle in its manifest on calibration and both held inputs.
coverage: Divide observed profiled visits by the paired full sampler's total eligible visits. Require at least 90% on every repetition of each held-out input, using exact integer counts. Separately report each input, all eight real inputs, the same-path control, the changed-path control, both control inputs and all ten. Low coverage is a feature-fidelity failure even if the run is fast.

cost.primary: Sum child wait4 user-plus-system CPU and elapsed parent process CPU over the entire operational interval. The interval includes the common timed ELF digest, appropriate lookup/cache validation, launch, polling, wait/stdio handling, and, on calibration, profile construction and persistence. The separate component CPU timers are included once in parent CPU. Exclude offline study checks. Preserve all repetitions.
cost.sensitivity: Repeat comparisons with child-only CPU. Additionally show the operational result when an unprofiled baseline can omit its measured common preflight ELF hash, leaving the profiled and profile-creation costs intact. Report measured elapsed workflow wall time descriptively with identical pairs.
cost.statistics: Use signed candidate-minus-base paired CPU differences and candidate/base ratios, and divide summed candidate time by summed base time for pooled ratios. Record each input and the frozen populations. Primary gates use unrounded workflow CPU sums. For profiled versus full require >=3% pooled savings and <=2% regression on every input. For profiled versus live require <=5% pooled overhead and <=10% on each input. Score the eight real cases separately from the two control cases; publish each control direction and the combined ten as descriptive populations. Do not discard outliers or convert a timing pass to a coverage pass.

amortization.baseline: Full sampling on every required input, including a first required calibration input if one is shared. These break-even results compare resource expenditure against full sampling. Each held input under an ELF has equal weight; use the arithmetic mean of all full-minus-profiled operational CPU differences under that ELF. Because each input has six repetitions, this is also the equal-weight mean of the per-input means. Report distinct same-path and switched-path scenarios as well as the control mixture.
amortization.online: When the full calibration input itself is an already required job, the full run and common preflight hash occur in both strategies. The measured incremental cost is the first profile's construction and persistence CPU, build_cpu_ns. When mean savings per subsequent required input is positive, report the smallest count N of subsequent inputs such that N times mean savings covers this initial cost, rounding upward; also report 1+N total required graded executions.
amortization.standalone: When the calibration input is an extra run, charge its entire measured workflow CPU, including parent, hashing, full child execution, selection and write. Divide by the same mean savings and round upward. N counts required scored inputs after the extra calibration.
amortization.sensitivity_no_baseline_hash: If full could omit hashing, subtract the full arm's measured hash CPU from every held full baseline. For online calibration charge its measured hash plus build; standalone still charges the whole calibration. Report the separate amortization under this assumption.
amortization.nonpositive: If mean savings is zero or negative, report no finite amortization instead of dividing or substituting a large count. Report coverage next to the cost-only break-even when the learned sites fail to represent the held workload. Six repeats and a single calibration provide a point estimate only.

authority: Experimental single-threaded x86-64 diagnostic on five real binaries and a deliberately switched-path control on one machine. Selection depends on the first input and executable digest. No native-time accuracy or trusted grading qualification.
